title:
Comment of Lindsay Standish in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/22/2026

documents.name: 151797.txt
documents.text:
Lindsay Standish, Anchorage, AK.
I strongly oppose the proposed DeepGreen underwater data center in Cook Inlet. Installing the turbines will create hydroacoustic noise pollution that threatens local marine life, including sensitive salmon and endangered beluga whale populations. 

The use of our Oceans as thermal waste heat sinks risks creating a warm-water plume in the narrow Forelands corridor, potentially disrupting vital salmon migration routes, all while poisoning them with copper. Our salmon populations are already under stress. This is an unacceptable risk. (Why, in a state with an energy crisis we aren’t talking about harvesting this waste heat is beyond me.)

Energy-intensive data centers are inherently unhealthy for society and have no place in Alaska. Our wilderness is the single most valuable resource we have, and we must safeguard it. It is unacceptable to gamble with the pristine natural heritage that future generations deserve to inherit. We should not sacrifice Cook Inlet's delicate ecosystem to power industrial computing. I urge FERC to reject this project and preserve Alaska’s untouched environment.
